target_customer: Small and medium businesses and teams that run on Google Apps and need shared tasks, events and files
problem: Teams that live in Gmail and Google Apps scatter tasks, events and documents across tools, so work gets lost in the inbox.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for teams (paid plans described as revenue source by TechCrunch in 2012)
product_category: Collaboration and project management inside Google Apps

founders.name: Niccolo Pantucci
previous_startups: Taskforce (task management app, outcome not found)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2012 and 2013 name him as founder and co-founder. Aggregator profiles mention education and past employers but I did not open a primary source, so those fields are left empty.

founders.name: Courtland Allen
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists him under Former Founders without stating his role; later founded Indie Hackers (per the YC page).

exit.reason: Not public. YC lists the company as inactive; Seedtable lists it as wound down.

competitors.name: Producteev
competitors.what: Task management service that added Google Tasks sync and an Outlook plugin

technical_complexity.rationale: A web app plus a Gmail gadget and Google Calendar and Docs integrations; TechCrunch 2012 describes a two-way calendar sync and a Chrome app, which is ordinary integration work for a team of two.

defensibility.rationale: Little beyond integrations with Google Apps; the Google Apps Marketplace listing gave distribution but nothing stopped rivals from building the same Gmail gadget.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Asana launched publicly on 2011-11-02 and Basecamp and Yammer were already large; TechCrunch 2012 describes Siasto positioned against them. Google was not reported to copy it.

market_need_then: Google Apps adoption among small businesses was rising and TechCrunch (2012) reported more than 5,000 teams signed up within 60 days of the April 2012 launch, which shows demand for task tools tied to the inbox.

branding.domain_note: Used siasto.com (exact .com). The domain now redirects to a brand-name marketplace listing, so the site is dead.
branding.brand_signature: Nicknamed 'The Pinterest For Work' by some users, per TechCrunch 2012
branding.community_and_virality: Among the most-installed apps in the Google Apps Marketplace in mid 2012 per TechCrunch.

brand_strength.rationale: Only the Pinterest for Work nickname and a Google Apps Marketplace feature are documented; no logo, mascot or brand coverage found.

outcome_analysis: Siasto came out of YC W11 from the founders of Taskforce, launched publicly in April 2012 and reported 5,000 teams and fast revenue growth within two months, then raised $750K in August 2013 to go mobile and into Asia. It is now listed as inactive, but no source states when or why it closed, so the cause is not public and no failure factors are asserted. Crowded competition from Asana, Basecamp and Yammer is context, not a documented cause.
notes: The 2011-08 seed round rests on a single database (Seedtable) with no amount. CB Insights reports $770K total raised, which is $20K above the $750K TechCrunch round and the gap is unexplained; that figure rests on one database. The 2013 TechCrunch article does not state a stage label, so the stage is other; Seedtable and CB Insights call it seed. The public launch was April 2012 while YC lists batch Winter 2011, so the competitor as_of is set to 2011-05, after the batch, using the only dated pre-Asana rival found; Asana (Nov 2011) and Basecamp appear only in 2012 sources and are noted here, not listed. Funding total is not stated by the company. Cause of closure not found.
